abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's actual variation well: one card component, one home view shared across runtimes, one species-mapping pipeline, one generic table sorter. Adding an Items section reuses the data layer and components wholesale; only the bespoke page function would be copied from movePage, which keeps it at 4 rather than 5.

findings.issue: All six page renderers live in one 459-line file separated only by comment banners; every page edit and every feature removal collides in the same module, and movesSection alone is ~110 lines mixing fetching, grouping, sorting and markup.
findings.suggestion: Split into src/server/pages/{home,pokemon,move,ability,type,not-found}.js with renderPage importing them; movesSection's data assembly could move into api.js next to the other data pipelines.

findings.issue: Sprite derivation is duplicated: home prefers pokemon.sprites.front_default with a spriteUrl fallback, while every other card list (api.js:143-147) always constructs spriteUrl and never handles a null front_default — a sprite bug fix must land twice and the two paths already behave differently.
findings.suggestion: Extract one resolveSpeciesSprite(pokemon, speciesId) helper used by both buildSummaries and speciesForPokemonRef.

findings.issue: Build output is committed: .gitignore only covers node_modules, and app/dist/ (with hashed Vite assets) sits in the tree, so PRs will carry stale generated code that reviewers can mistake for source.
findings.suggestion: Add app/dist/ (or dist/) to .gitignore and delete it from the tree.

findings.issue: The short_effect-then-flavor-then-em-dash effect extraction is duplicated verbatim in abilityPage (pages.js:331).
findings.suggestion: Add an englishShortEffect(record) helper to shared/format.js next to latestEnglishFlavor and call it from both pages.

findings.issue: The client depends on hardcoded element IDs (species-data, filter-search, filter-type, filter-generation, results, game-select) that are defined as string literals in server templates (pages.js:56-74, :217); a rename compiles fine and fails silently at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Keep the IDs in one shared constant module (e.g. shared/ids.js) imported by both the templates and main.js, or add a data-* hook convention documented in one place.

findings.issue: Four hand-rolled memoization patterns (cache:15, listCache, summariesPromise:70, speciesMapPromise:121) each with their own error-eviction logic; a caching-policy change (TTL, invalidation, size bound) means editing all four.
findings.suggestion: Extract one memoize(key, loader) helper and route getJson, getList and the two summary promises through it.

findings.issue: The entire 1025-species summary array is serialized into the HTML and re-parsed by the client (main.js:14), coupling server and client on an implicit shape contract with no shared type or schema definition.
findings.suggestion: At minimum, define the summary shape once (JSDoc typedef in shared/home-view.js) and note the contract next to both the serializer and the parser; consider sending only what the client can't recompute.

findings.issue: speciesCardsForPokemonRefs accepts three ref shapes (ref.url ?? ref.pokemon?.url ?? ref) plus an extraFor callback, a flexible but underspecified seam that makes the function's contract hard to read and easy to misuse.
findings.suggestion: Normalize refs at the call sites (pages.js already knows each shape) and take a flat array of {url, isHidden}-style records instead.

summary: This is a well-factored vanilla app: pure shared modules, a single card component, one home view reused by SSR and the client, and an isolated data layer, so most fixes and extensions touch one or two files. The main editability liabilities are the monolithic 459-line pages.js, a handful of duplicated derivations (sprite, effect text, list ordering, caching) that a fix must chase down, and committed build output. It reads like code a small team could own for years with modest refactoring.
